#!/usr/bin/env bash

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

PROJECT_DIR="$(pwd -P)"
DIST_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/dist"
WEB_DIR="${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:-/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-web}"
PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export PORT

now_ms() { date +%s%3N; }

run_timed() {
  local label="$1"
  shift
  local start end status=0
  start="$(now_ms)"
  "$@" || status=$?
  end="$(now_ms)"
  printf '[timing] %s: %d ms\n' "$label" "$((end - start))"
  return "$status"
}

install_dependencies() {
  if [[ -f package-lock.json ]]; then
    npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
  else
    npm install --no-audit --no-fund
  fi
}

write_deployment_output() {
  mkdir -p "$WEB_DIR"
  node -e '
    const { writeFileSync } = require("node:fs");
    const [output, project, directory] = process.argv.slice(1);
    writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify({ project, directory }) + "\n");
  ' "$WEB_DIR/deployment-output.json" "$PROJECT_DIR" "$DIST_DIR"
}

[[ "$PORT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "PORT must be a number, got: $PORT" >&2; exit 1; }

if [[ ! -d node_modules/three ]] || [[ package-lock.json -nt node_modules/.package-lock.json ]]; then
  run_timed "install dependencies" install_dependencies
else
  printf '[timing] install dependencies: skipped (node_modules up to date)\n'
fi

# Build a self-contained static directory. The project serves prebuilt files and
# needs no runtime framework, so a clean copy is the build step.
run_timed "clean static build" rm -rf "$DIST_DIR"
run_timed "create static build" mkdir -p "$DIST_DIR"
run_timed "copy static files" cp -R index.html styles.css src vendor assets "$DIST_DIR"/
run_timed "verify static build" test -f "$DIST_DIR/index.html"

run_timed "write deployment-output.json" write_deployment_output

printf '[timing] serve: starting static server on port %s from %s\n' "$PORT" "$DIST_DIR"
cd "$DIST_DIR"
exec /usr/bin/time -p node ../server.mjs
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
PROJECT_DIR="${PROJECT_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR}"

: "${CAPTURE_URL:?Set CAPTURE_URL to the preview URL to capture.}"
: "${CAPTURE_DIR:?Set CAPTURE_DIR to an output directory outside the project.}"

now_ms() { date +%s%3N; }

run_timed() {
  local label="$1"
  shift
  local start end status=0
  start="$(now_ms)"
  "$@" || status=$?
  end="$(now_ms)"
  printf '[timing] %s: %d ms\n' "$label" "$((end - start))"
  return "$status"
}

case "$CAPTURE_URL" in
  http://*|https://*) ;;
  *) echo "CAPTURE_URL must start with http:// or https://: $CAPTURE_URL" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

PROJECT_DIR="$(realpath -m "$PROJECT_DIR")"
CAPTURE_DIR="$(realpath -m "$CAPTURE_DIR")"
case "$CAPTURE_DIR/" in
  "$PROJECT_DIR/"*)
    echo "CAPTURE_DIR must be outside the source project: $CAPTURE_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

run_timed "create capture directory" mkdir -p "$CAPTURE_DIR"
run_timed "capture desktop and mobile preview" env \
  CAPTURE_URL="$CAPTURE_URL" \
  CAPTURE_DIR="$CAPTURE_DIR" \
  PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR" \
  node "$SCRIPT_DIR/capture.mjs"

## Objective
- Build and finish the browser game into a complete, playable experience from the current prototype.
- Continue the existing F1 track drawing and racing project and complete the remaining gameplay, UI, and validation work.

## Requirements
- Build a complete, playable game now; no clarifying questions.
- Reasonable assumptions are allowed and should be noted briefly at the end.
- Screenshot verification: save small JPEGs at 1280px or less wide and read only the latest one.
- Keep the game usable on desktop and touch/mobile layouts.

## Decisions
- The project is a browser-based F1 track drawing and racing game with a menu, garage, draw flow, race, and results loop.
- The priority is finishing the playable loop and responsiveness rather than adding unrelated systems.
- Playwright on `http://localhost:3002` was used to validate the game flow and layout changes.
- Responsive/mobile fixes were treated as essential to complete the game.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project structure and game flow were inspected and mapped.
- The existing draw/garage/menu/race/results flow was validated and used as the base for completion work.
- Responsive UI fixes were applied for short/mobile screens, including touch controls, pause/results modal overflow, and menu layout issues.
- Race and results checks were run in desktop and mobile viewports.
- Track preview/analysis logic was inspected and tuned to improve corner/straight detection and preview validity.
- Browser verification covered the menu, garage, drawing workflow, race loop, and results presentation.

### Active
- Final polishing pass for gameplay completeness and responsiveness across screen sizes.
- Re-checking the race-results and touch-control behaviors after the latest UI fixes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run a final browser pass from menu → draw → build → race → results.
2. Confirm the latest JPEG captures reflect the intended final state and the UI remains usable on desktop and touch devices.
3. Fix any remaining edge-case issues in track validation or race finish presentation if the final pass exposes them.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: app shell and screen structure.
- `styles.css`: responsive UI, touch controls, modals, and layout fixes.
- `src/main.js`: game state, screen transitions, race lifecycle, UI events, and results flow.
- `src/track.js`: track preview analysis, corner/straight detection, and geometry utilities.
- `src/draw.js`: track drawing flow and example tracks.
- `src/world.js`: world/state rendering and simulation logic.
- `src/car.js`: car physics and input behavior.
- `server.mjs`: local app server.
- `package.json`: scripts and dependencies.
- `capture.mjs`: screenshot capture helper.
- `README.md`: project overview.
- `startup.sh`: startup helper.
- `start.sh`: app start helper.
- `capture.sh`: capture script.
- `.omgithub/checkpoint.json`: saved checkpoint state.

## Important Context
- The game is served locally at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright verification used Chrome and saved JPEG snapshots under `/tmp/opencode/*.jpg`.
- The app already reaches a functional race completion and results state.
- The main remaining work is final validation polish and any last responsive edge-case fixes.

# 🚀 APEX INK — Draw it. Race it.

A browser-based track builder racer. Sketch a closed circuit with a mouse or a fingertip, and APEX INK paves it into a 3D world with kerbs, run-off, scenery, and a full grid of AI rivals. Then race it.

## Play

```bash
npm install
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
```

Any static file server works too — the game ships with its own copy of Three.js in `vendor/`.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steer | `A` / `D` or `←` / `→` | Left / right pads |
| Throttle / brake override | `W` / `S` | GAS / BRAKE |
| Handbrake | `SPACE` | — |
| Camera | `C` | — |
| Recover to track | `R` | — |
| Pause | `ESC` | Pause button |

The car drives its own throttle and brakes; you focus on the racing line unless you override with `W` / `S`.

## Features

- Freehand circuit drawing with live length, corner, straight, and run-off analysis.
- Closed-loop validation that rejects self-intersecting scribbles.
- Procedural 3D world, kerbs, scenery, start gantry, and dynamic lighting.
- One to ten laps, zero to nine AI racers, three rival difficulty levels.
- Livery studio with per-part paint, presets, colour wheel, hex input, and stickers.
- Chase and onboard cameras, live standings, sector map, DRS, lap timing, and a full classification screen.
- Responsive desktop, phone, tablet, and landscape layouts with on-screen touch controls.
- Synthesised engine and UI audio, saved circuits, and best-lap records.

- Finish the game without clarification; use reasonable assumptions and briefly note them.

- Prioritize the existing menu, garage, drawing, racing, and results loop over unrelated new systems.

### Completed
- Completed and validated the full loop: menu → garage → draw → build → race → pause/results → race again or new circuit.
